newsitem.title: ITALY: Benetton profits rise and hopes for more.
newsitem.headline: Benetton profits rise and hopes for more.

text.p: Italian clothing company Benetton on Monday reported an increase of nine percent in first half 1996 profits and saw no reason why profits should not continue to rise by that amount during in the second half.

The company, based in Ponzano in north-eastern Italy and with franchised stores in 120 countries, said that its group consolidated first half net profits rose to 115.8 billion lire ($76 million) while turnover was largely flat.

"We are confidence we can match the same turnover of last year, and see no reason for profits to go down. Our goal is to see second half profits show the same increase as in the first half," said Carlo Gilardi managing director of Benetton.

Gilardi told Reuters that Benetton had increased its prices a little less than average inflation levels, and while labour costs had also gone up, the group had not suffered significantly from fluctuations in raw material prices like wool and cotton.
Earlier this month, group chairman Luciano Benetton had said first half revenue would be flat and net profits show only a slight increase with trading conditions remaining difficult.

Benetton's costs in the first half suffered from the high value of the lira with 80 percent of its produce manufactured in Italy, but it made profits from its foreign exchange activities to largely offset the strength of the Italian currency.

With first half sales only marginally ahead at 1.47 trillion lire and the cost of sales rising to 871.5 billion lire from 832.9 billion lire, group operating profits fell to 203.6 billion lire for a previous 321.7 billion.
The operating profit slide slimmed profit margins to 13.9 percent from 15.8 percent, but Benetton's Gilardi said a margin of around 14 percent was still a "fairly good long-term figure".

The group benefited from a 39.4 billion lire foreign exchange gain due to the strength of the lira in the first-half after a loss of 22.8 billion lire on its foreign exchange activities in the previous first half.

Gilardi also confirmed that the group expected to be debt free or have a small cash balance at the end of the year helped by the group's strong cash flow. Finance charges fell to 12.6 billion lire from 27.2 billion as the debt shrank to 235.5 billion lire from 489.7 billion at June 30 1995.

Analysts said that the cost of sales was also increasing as Benetton took more of its production in-house and invested heavily in manufacturing, but the fall in the profit margin was still more than expected at the operating level.

"On the one hand the results were not as good as expected, but this is balanced against the news that the Sportsystem group is going to be floated," said Michael Pacitti Italian equity analysts at brokerage house HSBC James Capel.
Earlier, Benetton said it might float its entire Sportsystem division on the New York stock market by the end of 1997, which includes the Rollerblade skates and Prince tennis brand.

Sportsystem is held by the Benetton family group Edizione Holdings, which itself holds a majority stake in Benetton, and there had been market talk that Edizione may sell Sportsystem to the Benetton group at an inflated price.

Benetton shares shed 3.76 percent to close at 17,150 lire on worries over the profit margin fall and the longer term impact that a strong lira would have on its business in which two- thirds of sales are made outside Itlay.
Benetton said it invested 40 billion lire during the first half in its principle trading brands of United Colors of Benetton, upmarket Sisley, childrenwear 012 and new born wear Zerotondo.

Earlier this month, Benetton opened its largest ever store in London's West End in the Oxford Street shopping district, and added that it plans to open a similar-sized store in New York's Fifth Avenue at the end of October, ($1=1,522 lire)
